outlier.evidence: Ratings 6 to 8 around a mean of 7.0. Reviewer_rSNF's 8 is one point above three 7s; without it the mean is 6.75. Reviewer_adW2's 6 is the lowest and still recommends acceptance. No single review decides the outcome. rSNF's 8 at confidence 5 is weakly supported: the review is mostly open technical objections (Signorini condition dropped, SCS on a singular A, no gradSim comparison, DiffTaichi wins billiards, limitations 'a bit limited'), and rSNF never replied to the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: The only test data for comparing trajectory error is generated by the proposed model itself, so there is zero model mismatch.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.2 (lines 212-218) builds all training, evaluation and test sets by simulation, and the authors' reply ('CM generated data') confirms the simulator is the proposed model. LCP-generated data appear only in the Robustness paragraph (lines 297-305), which reports learned contact properties, not trajectory errors. The authors agreed and added LCP-data trajectory errors in the discussion; BP5-e error rose from 2.34e-5 to 7.35e-4.

checkable_claims.claim: There is no improvement in the Rope environment, so the method may not scale to many contacts.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 2: on Rope the CM models sit near 3e-3 and the baselines near 5e-3 to 8e-3, about 2-fold, against gaps of two or more orders of magnitude on BP5-e, CP3-e and Gyro-e. 'No improvement' overstates a small gain. The authors first answered that the methods win 'by around an order of magnitude', then conceded 'around 2-fold instead of an order of magnitude' at D=400.

checkable_claims.claim: The Signorini complementarity condition between normal impulses and velocities is ignored.
checkable_claims.evidence: Problems (5) and (7) constrain the impulses only by the friction cone (3), non-negativity (4) and Poisson's inequality (6); there is no complementarity constraint. The authors conceded it is an approximation, as in MuJoCo, and the camera-ready adds that note to Section 3.2.

checkable_claims.claim: DiffTaichi performs better than the proposed model on the billiards task.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 322-324: DiffTaichi 'has better convergence in learning, as shown in Fig 6(c)'. The authors attributed it to their lack of time-of-impact handling with RK4.

checkable_claims.claim: The code is not included in this submission.
checkable_claims.evidence: Checklist 3(a) answers [No]: 'We will publish our code after the review period'.

checkable_claims.claim: Macklin et al. [35] is not discussed in the related work, and IPC is missing.
checkable_claims.evidence: [35] appears only inside the range [31-36] (line 77) and at line 326; IPC is absent from the references. The camera-ready discusses both in Section 1.1.

checkable_claims.claim: [34] does test energy conservation for its contact model, against the paper's statement that prior simulators' energy prediction 'has not been evaluated'.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 83-84 make the statement. The authors conceded that Fig. 6 in [34] shows total energy over time and narrowed their claim to energy of learned models. [34] itself is not in the files.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_aKSy wrote on 2021-08-31 'I increase my score to 7'; the authors replied on 2021-09-01 that they 'still see the score 5 instead of 7'; the review was edited on 2021-09-01 and now ends 'post rebuttal: ... I change my score to 7'. Reviewer_GQFZ wrote on 2021-08-17 'I'm raising my score to 7' and edited the review that day; the earlier score is not visible. Reviewer_snrk (2021-09-02): 'I maintain my score to 7, conditioned on' two manuscript changes. Reviewer_adW2 edited on 2021-08-05, before the first author responses (2021-08-07), and stayed at 6. Reviewer_rSNF never edited or replied.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: aKSy asked for rope results across contact counts, network sizes and training-set sizes. The authors ran all three, conceded the D=400 gain is 'around 2-fold instead of an order of magnitude' and promised a scalability limitation; aKSy raised 5 to 7 and asked for the limitation in the conclusion. GQFZ accepted the target-velocity rule (Appendix G), the claim of insensitivity and the code-release plan. adW2 rejected the authors' overfitting reading of the data-scaling table ('there is an optimization problem rather than an over-fitting problem') and did not answer the corrected LCP-data table; adW2 kept 6. snrk accepted that gradSim and ADD code was unreleased and asked for written pros and cons against [35] and IPC. The camera-ready adds IPC and Macklin et al. to Section 1.1, the Signorini note to Section 3.2 and a contact-rich scalability limitation to Section 6.

ac.evidence: 'All reviewers recommend acceptance and by the end of the rebuttal process became satisfied with the additional experiments and clarifications by the authors.' All five ratings are 6 or above (mean 7.0). The meta-review also notes the contact-rich scalability limit from aKSy's thread. 'Satisfied' overstates adW2, who disputed the authors' reading of the baseline results and did not reply to the last update. The AC gives no own reading of the paper.

main_reasons_for_decision: Unanimous ratings of 6 or above (mean 7.0); the AC accepted on the consensus

Contribution credited as joint learning of system and contact properties inside Lagrangian/Hamiltonian networks (Reviewer_snrk: 'unique contributions in its machine learning experiments'; Reviewer_aKSy and Reviewer_GQFZ: novel combination)
Rebuttal experiments on rope scaling, data scaling and LCP-generated data raised Reviewer_aKSy from 5 to 7 and Reviewer_GQFZ to 7
Missing simulator comparisons, no real data and limited contact-rich scalability treated as limitations to document, not reasons to reject

outlier.evidence: Ratings split 6, 6 against 4, 4, 4 (mean 4.8). No single reviewer departs from the rest; without Reviewer_edmT's 4 the mean is 5.0, still below the threshold. Neither 6 is a champion: Reviewer_hJGq names significance as the main limitation and Reviewer_i24Y wants planning and control experiments.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: One paragraph, 1 hour, confidence 5 ('checked the math/other details carefully'). It says 'The authors primarily compare their method to a standard LCP-based simulator' and that benchmarks are 'performed against existing simulators'. The main comparisons (Figures 2-5) are against MLP and Interaction Network baselines on data from the paper's own model; LCP is only a failed baseline (lines 247-251) and a robustness data source (lines 297-305). No reply to the rebuttal.

Partly. It says the contact model is 'soft' due to 'the convex formulation that is regularized'; the main model CM is unregularized and only the CMr variant adds R = eps*I (lines 230-233). It doubts 3D scaling because rotations need quaternions or MRPs; the paper uses Cartesian coordinates with explicit constraints (lines 103-110) and runs 3D gyroscope tasks. No reply after the authors corrected the 3D point. Its other points (toy systems, no Nimble comparison, no real data) are accurate.

checkable_claims.claim: The authors primarily compare their method to a standard LCP-based simulator.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.2 baselines are MLP-CD-CLNN, IN-CP-CLNN and IN-CP-SP, trained on data from the proposed model. The LCP baseline [26] failed with NaN gradients (lines 247-251); LCP data appear only in the one-paragraph robustness test (lines 297-305).

checkable_claims.claim: The authors use the LCP method's linearization to explain some of their observed errors.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 301-305 attribute the less accurate Gyro contact properties learned from LCP data (COR 0.822 instead of 0.800) to the LCP's polyhedral relaxation of the friction cone. These are parameter errors, not prediction errors.

checkable_claims.claim: The method is not validated on real data.
checkable_claims.evidence: All data in Sections 4 and 5 are simulated. The authors to edmT: 'We agree that we didn't test our model on real world data, but this is not the main focus of this work.'

checkable_claims.claim: The contact model is 'soft' due to the convex formulation that is regularized.
checkable_claims.evidence: CM sets up (5) and (7) 'exactly as stated'; only CMr adds a regularizer R = eps*I (lines 230-233), and 'In most tasks, CM outperforms CMr' (line 258).

checkable_claims.claim: Most of the work is in 2D.
checkable_claims.evidence: Table 1: six of eight tasks are 2D; only Gyro-e and Gyro are 3D.

checkable_claims.claim: Scaling to 3D is doubtful because rotations need an orientation representation (quaternions, MRPs) unsuited to the convex contact problem.
checkable_claims.evidence: The paper uses Cartesian coordinates with explicit constraints from [11] (lines 103-110), so no orientation parameterization enters the contact problem, and the 3D gyroscope tasks train without issue (Figure 2, Table 2).

checkable_claims.claim: In the billiard simulation, DiffTaichi regresses much faster than the proposed method.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 322-324 and Figure 6(c): DiffTaichi 'has better convergence in learning'.

checkable_claims.claim: The parameter-estimation experiments do not compare with DiffTaichi or other differentiable simulators.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 4.2 lists only learned baselines (MLP and Interaction Network variants); DiffTaichi appears only in the billiards planning task (Section 5).

checkable_claims.claim: [29, 30] already learn contact properties and use them for real-world robot manipulation, so line 74's 'has yet to be tested' should be reconsidered.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 72-74 group [26-30] under 'their performance on learning the contact properties has yet to be tested'. The authors conceded that [29][30] 'did learn the coefficient of friction' and narrowed the claim to accuracy not being reported.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_BwHT, Reviewer_i24Y and Reviewer_edmT never edited their reviews. Reviewer_hJGq edited on 2021-07-17, before the 2021-08-10 responses. Reviewer_i24Y (2021-09-03): 'I am inclined to keep my original score.' Reviewer_Kv95 edited on 2021-09-01 with no discussion post and no post-rebuttal note in the text, so any change to its 4 is invisible. No other reviewer replied.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The B rebuttal was text only and conceded the main gaps: real data is 'not the main focus of this work', the contact model 'is indeed modified from previous works', locomotion and manipulation are untested, and robot-scale experiments are left out 'Due to time constraints'. It corrected BwHT's 3D concern (Cartesian extended-body representation, gyroscope example) and argued that DiffTaichi's billiards code has no friction. No detractor answered. i24Y kept 6 because 'the evaluation can be improved with planning/control problems'. The experiments run for Committee A (LCP-generated validation data, data scaling, rope scaling) were never posted to B.

ac.evidence: Three of five ratings are 4 (mean 4.8). The three reasons map onto specific reviews: 'a combination of existing proposals' (edmT, Kv95, BwHT); 'serial-link manipulators, quadrupeds, and humanoids' is copied from BwHT's 'Compelling examples' point; 'validated with real data as opposed to data from other simulators' paraphrases edmT, whose description of the data is wrong for the main experiments, which use the paper's own model. The meta-review does not mention the two 6s or the authors' corrections.

Only simple simulated systems; no serial-link manipulators, quadrupeds or humanoids (Reviewer_BwHT, Reviewer_i24Y; AC)
No validation on real data (Reviewer_edmT, Reviewer_BwHT; AC)
No comparison with other differentiable simulators such as DiffTaichi, Nimble or NeuralSim (Reviewer_Kv95, Reviewer_BwHT, Reviewer_hJGq)
Three 4s and two lukewarm 6s (mean 4.8); no detractor engaged with the rebuttal

issues_only_a: All trajectory-error test data come from the proposed model itself: zero model mismatch (Reviewer_adW2)
Small gain on the contact-rich rope (about 2-fold) and scalability with contact count and data (Reviewer_aKSy)
Signorini condition not enforced; SCS and CvxpyLayers on a singular A; mixed acceleration-based and time-stepping integration (Reviewer_rSNF, Reviewer_adW2)
Penetration target velocity is a heuristic with untested sensitivity; code not supplied (Reviewer_GQFZ)
Baselines may be under-optimized: training loss oscillates, an optimization rather than overfitting problem (Reviewer_adW2)
Macklin et al. [35] and IPC not discussed (Reviewer_snrk)
Short energy-conservation horizons; friction parameters from LCP and cone models not comparable (Reviewer_rSNF)
issues_only_b: No demonstrations on robot systems such as serial-link manipulators, quadrupeds or humanoids (Reviewer_BwHT, Reviewer_i24Y, AC)
Missing Nimble (LCP) and spring-based baselines (Reviewer_BwHT) and DiffTaichi parameter estimation (Reviewer_Kv95)
Line 74 overclaims: [29, 30] and [36] already learn contact parameters (Reviewer_hJGq)
SCS returns subgradients that may not help discover new contact sequences (Reviewer_BwHT)
3D rotation representation (Reviewer_BwHT; answered by the paper's Cartesian coordinates)
Robot bodies approximated as 3D points; convexity assumption for real problems (Reviewer_i24Y)
shared_issues: Novelty by combination of CHNN/CLNN, a MuJoCo-like contact model and CvxpyLayers (A: Reviewer_aKSy and Reviewer_GQFZ call it a novel combination, GQFZ 'incremental'; B: Reviewer_edmT, Reviewer_Kv95 and Reviewer_BwHT call novelty unclear)
No comparison with other differentiable simulators or contact models (A: Reviewer_rSNF gradSim, Reviewer_snrk [35] and IPC, Reviewer_adW2 soft contact; B: Reviewer_Kv95, Reviewer_BwHT, Reviewer_hJGq)
No real-world data (A: Reviewer_adW2 'ideally', Reviewer_snrk as future work; B: Reviewer_edmT and Reviewer_BwHT as a requirement)
DiffTaichi converges faster on the billiards task (A: Reviewer_rSNF; B: Reviewer_Kv95)
No control inputs; planning only as initial-condition optimization (A: Reviewer_rSNF; B: Reviewer_i24Y)
Line 83 overstates that prior simulators ignore energy (A: Reviewer_adW2 citing [34]; B: Reviewer_hJGq)
Method needs an overview diagram (A: Reviewer_aKSy, Reviewer_GQFZ; B: Reviewer_hJGq)
verdict: Both committees saw the same paper and the same weaknesses: a combination of known parts (CHNN/CLNN, a MuJoCo-like convex contact model, CvxpyLayers), simple simulated systems, only learned baselines (MLP, Interaction Network) in the learning experiments, no real data, and a loss to DiffTaichi on the one head-to-head task. Reviewers mirror each other across committees: Reviewer_GQFZ (A, 7) called the contribution 'incremental' and Reviewer_hJGq (B, 6) named significance as the main limitation; Reviewer_adW2 (A, 6) and Reviewer_edmT (B, 4) both wanted data the model did not generate; Reviewer_rSNF (A, 8) and Reviewer_Kv95 (B, 4) both noted the DiffTaichi result and asked for simulator comparisons. Committee A credited joint learning of dynamics and contact parameters inside energy-conserving networks as new and treated the gaps as limitations. Committee B judged the paper as a robotics simulator, asked for robot systems, simulator baselines and real data, and gave three 4s; its two 6s were lukewarm. Engagement widened the gap. A's reviewers asked follow-ups, the authors ran new experiments (rope scaling, data scaling, LCP-generated validation data), and Reviewer_aKSy (5 to 7) and Reviewer_GQFZ (to 7) raised their scores. B's detractors never replied, never saw those experiments, and read a rebuttal that conceded the gaps. B's AC built the meta-review from Reviewer_BwHT and Reviewer_edmT, including edmT's wrong description of the data as coming from other simulators. B's misreadings (edmT on the LCP comparison, BwHT on regularization and 3D) did not decide the case; the decisive facts are true. The split is the acceptance bar each reviewer draw applied to the same facts.
